Adjust the two core toggles here, with defaults and local retention kept on the same page.
Defaults: Enable telemetry = Off. Enable privacy guard = On.
Even with telemetry off, OpenCray still keeps local settings, workspace access state, consent choices, and recent audit history on this device until a later clear-data flow removes them.
Default: Off. Turning telemetry off blocks outbound telemetry, but local settings, approvals, and recent audit entries remain stored on this device.
Local redaction stays enabled for eligible analytics and audit details.
Eligible analytics and audit details can use full local detail.
Default: On. Privacy guard changes what later telemetry may include, while local retention still keeps the current setting and recent audit history on-device.
Keep the key risk boundaries and release-critical warnings in one place for quick review.
Compare the tradeoffs between Safe, Auto, and Developer here before switching modes.
This section only describes rollback that is verified for local checkpoints.
This section mirrors the same defaults and retention rules shown in settings.
Defaults: Enable telemetry = Off. Enable privacy guard = On.
Keep V1 boundaries explicit so future ideas do not look like shipped runtime support.
Safe mode keeps approval prompts in front of sensitive actions so OpenCray favors review over speed when the risk surface grows.
Use this when you want the lowest-risk default path.
Auto mode reduces interruptions and can continue through more approved flows automatically, so mistakes can travel farther before someone notices.
Auto mode can reduce prompts, but hard denials still stop protected or path-blocked actions.
Developer mode can expose high-risk operations and reduce prompts for debugging or power use.
Developer mode does not override hard denials. Protected-file, path, and other hard policy denials still stop the action.
Guaranteed only for local filesystem checkpoints
Rollback is guaranteed only for local filesystem checkpoints created by OpenCray on this device.
Use rollback as a local safety net, not as a universal undo system.
Remote and external effects are not guaranteed
Rollback is local-only, not guaranteed for remote/external side effects such as shell commands, MCP actions, network requests, cloud changes, or any other external system change.
If something leaves the device or touches another system, rollback may not undo it.
Turning telemetry on allows anonymous product telemetry to leave the device. Leaving it off blocks outbound telemetry.
This setting persists on this device and can be changed later in TelemetryToggles or Settings > Telemetry and privacy.
Privacy guard keeps local redaction active for eligible analytics and audit details, even when telemetry stays off.
This setting persists on this device and can be changed later in TelemetryToggles or Settings > Telemetry and privacy.
V1 does not ship real Termux execution.
Current V1 runtime support remains in-app only, with Termux kept as a documented future phase rather than a shipped execution path.
Do not describe real Termux execution as available in this release.
Parallel agents, iOS, cloud sync, and public marketplace stay out of V1.
Multi-agent parallel execution, iOS client support, cloud collaboration sync, and a public marketplace review system are out of scope for V1.
These ideas can be planned later, but must not be implied as shipped now.
